Where it began

Pat Cummins was born at Westmead, in Sydney's west, on 8 May 1993, and was brought up in the Blue Mountains, at Mount Riverview. As a boy his hero was Brett Lee, and in time he got to share a dressing room with him for New South Wales and Australia. He learned the game at the Glenbrook-Blaxland club, moved up to first-grade cricket with Penrith in 2010, and in March 2011, aged 17, first played for New South Wales in a first-class match, against Tasmania.

The player

His Test career began in a rush. In November 2011, in only his fourth first-class match, he was picked against South Africa at Johannesburg, the youngest Australian Test cricketer since Ian Craig in 1953. He took 6 for 79 in the second innings, hit the four that won the match and was named man of the match. It was more than five years before his second Test, in March 2017, but from then on he was a fixture.

By October 2026 he had played 76 Tests and taken 326 wickets at 22.21, with 14 five-wicket innings and a best of 6 for 23. In 2019 he became the world's top-ranked Test bowler, the first Australian there since Glenn McGrath, and took 29 wickets in that summer's Ashes. In November 2021 he was made Australia's 47th Test captain, the first fast bowler to hold the job full-time. By October 2026 he had led them in 42 Tests, with 26 wins against 10 defeats.

What made him special

He kept on finding ways to win. Under him Australia won the World Test Championship final in 2023, the World Cup in India later that year after losing their first two games, a series in Pakistan on Australia's first visit there for 24 years, and the Border–Gavaskar Trophy in 2024–25 after a seven-year wait. In the 2025–26 Ashes he dismissed Joe Root for the 13th time, more often than any other bowler had.

His batting was more of a side project: 1,670 Test runs at 16.70, three fifties and a best of 64 not out. It had its moments, though. In the 2023 World Cup he made 12 from 68 balls while Glenn Maxwell supplied most of a 202-run stand against Afghanistan, which may be the most unselfish innings ever played.

Away from the middle

The honours piled up: the Allan Border Medal in 2019, the ICC's Test Cricketer of the Year award that same year, Wisden Cricketer of the Year in 2020, and in 2023 both the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy and Wisden's Leading Cricketer in the World. Between seasons he studied at the University of Technology, Sydney, and in 2017 he finished a business degree there. In rugby league his team is the Penrith Panthers.

And finally

The patient batter of that World Cup stand had another setting. In the 2022 Indian Premier League he reached fifty from 14 balls, equalling the fastest in the competition's history at the time. Bowlers running in at him were entitled to wonder which Cummins would turn up.
